reference: GNU coreutils fold from the runner's reference PATH for parity cases. The -c UTF-8 character-count contract is independently taken from /source/docs/sol-fold.md and strict UTF-8 byte encodings; Bash type/help metadata is asserted directly.
coverage: Default 80-column behavior and explicit-width wrapping, including an unterminated final line.
Byte mode over NUL, multibyte bytes, spaces, and tabs, with and without word wrapping.
Display-column handling of tabs, backspace, and carriage return in the C locale.
Space and tab word-wrap behavior, including words longer than the selected width.
Ordered file operands, empty files, repeated stdin operands, and per-file column reset.
A leading-dash filename protected by --, invalid width status, and continuation after a missing input file.
Bash type/help metadata and the documented -c scalar counting and malformed-byte preservation contract.
exclusions: GNU fold has no matching -c character-count option; that behavior is checked against the independent documented UTF-8 contract.
Locale-dependent non-ASCII display widths are not compared; parity display-column cases use ASCII and LC_ALL=C.
Incremental output while a producer remains open is deferred because this fixture runner has no concurrent open-producer or PTY driver.

cases.purpose: Confirm the candidate is exposed as a Bash builtin and Bash help metadata is available without treating metadata as operation coverage.
Compare the GNU default width and an explicit width on several short lines, including a final line without a newline.
cases.script:
printf 'alpha beta\nabcde\nq' > text
fold -w4 < text
fold < text

cases.purpose: Compare byte counting over NUL and UTF-8 bytes, including byte-boundary splitting and -bs blank handling.
cases.script:
printf 'A\000\303\251Z\none two\tX\n' > bytes
fold -b -w3 < bytes
fold -bs -w4 < bytes

cases.purpose: Compare ASCII display-column behavior for tab stops, backspace, and carriage-return column reset.
Compare -s breaking after the last eligible space or tab while still hard-wrapping long words.
cases.script:
printf 'alpha beta gamma
12345 67890
ab	cdEFG
' > words
fold -s -w6 < words

cases.purpose: Compare file order, an empty file, repeated stdin operands, and column reset when the preceding file lacks a final newline.
cases.script:
printf 'ab' > first
: > empty
printf 'cdef\n' > second
printf 'ghi jk\n' | fold -s -w3 first empty - second -

cases.purpose: Compare -- handling for a relative input filename that begins with a dash.
Retain GNU's invalid-width exit status and diagnostic behavior as a negative parity case.
Compare a missing input diagnostic and nonzero result while confirming a later valid file is still folded.
Check the documented -c rule that each valid UTF-8 scalar and each malformed byte counts as one, while preserving input bytes.
Verify that a completed folded line is delivered before the input producer closes, for both pipe and terminal output.
cases.reason: Requires a future isolated open-producer and PTY driver that can hold stdin open, send a width-overflowing prefix, and observe output before EOF; the current one-shot fixture runner captures output only after the script exits.
